reviews.review:
The lack of a fish-eye effect toggle is a huge letdown in an otherwise amazing game.
I purchased this game after waiting a long time, hoping that accessibility options like these would be present, especially since I had previously asked the developer about them. Effects such as fish-eye distortion, head bobbing, and extreme flashing lights are known to trigger epilepsy and other visual sensitivities. I genuinely cannot understand when developers fail to include toggles for these effects.
A toggle doesn’t mean turning off these features for everyone—it simply allows players who cannot handle them to enjoy the game safely. Unfortunately, this absence is a dealbreaker for me. My playtime was very short, as the effects nearly made me physically ill within the first minutes.
That said, I do appreciate that the head bob can be toggled, which is a nice touch. The game itself is awesome, but ill be asking for a refund, since most devs do not care about this kind of feedback. 
However, my review is specifically for those who, like me, cannot deal with these intense visual effects. This is a common issue in the Backrooms genre, and one that many developers seem to overlook.
I hope a toggle is added in the future. I also hope the developer doesn’t take this personally—my critique is not about the quality of the game, but about a basic accessibility feature that should be standard. These two simple options can make the game playable for a much wider audience.
